extracted.intended_audience: Community organizations and applicants to the Boulder County Climate Equity Fund (frontline community groups and project leaders seeking climate-related grants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting applications to the Boulder County Climate Equity Fund, covering eligibility, application steps, technical requirements for Tier 1 and Tier 2 grants, budgeting, timelines, documentation, and community engagement. Focused on serving frontline communities most impacted by climate change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of the Boulder County Climate Equity Fund eligibility criteria for projects to receive funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The session described which projects and applicants are eligible, emphasizing support for climate-related initiatives in frontline communities and outlining distinctions between Tier 1 and Tier 2 eligibility. Applicants should confirm they meet the fund's stated eligibility before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application process
rubrics_metrics.description: Details about the application process for the Climate Equity Fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The meeting covered steps to apply, deadlines, and submission procedures. Follow the fund's application instructions exactly, submit required forms by the stated deadlines, and use the specified submission channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical requirements (Tier 1 and Tier 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical requirements specific to both Tier 1 and Tier 2 grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The session reviewed technical requirements for each tier. Applicants should review tier-specific instructions (formats, file types, technical attachments) and ensure all technical submission requirements are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on preparing project budgets and answering budget-related questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants asked about budgeting; applicants should provide clear, itemized budgets, justify costs, align expenses with project activities, and follow any fund rules on allowable costs or caps per line item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions and guidance regarding project timelines and scheduling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The office hours covered timelines; applicants should propose realistic start/completion dates, milestones, and implementation schedules that fit the fund's grant period and reporting expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants asked about documentation; applicants should prepare and attach required documents (e.g., proof of eligibility, financial statements, letters of support, scopes of work) as specified by the fund to avoid incomplete applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project eligibility focus: serving frontline communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasis on serving communities most impacted by climate change (frontline communities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The session stressed that proposals should demonstrate how projects benefit frontline communities, describing target populations, needs, and how the project advances climate equity. Evidence of community need and impact increases competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear project goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance of articulating clear project goals and expected outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speakers emphasized clear, measurable goals; applicants should define objectives, expected results, and metrics for success so reviewers can assess project clarity and likely impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations around community engagement in project design and implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The meeting highlighted community engagement as important; applicants should describe how communities were involved in planning, include partnership or support letters where applicable, and explain strategies for meaningful engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding amounts and tier selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about funding amounts (up to $2.5 million total in 2025) and the two funding tiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The session provided details on total available funding and distinctions between Tier 1 and Tier 2 grant sizes. Applicants should select the tier matching their project scope and request appropriate funding amounts consistent with tier limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of how applications will be reviewed and selected for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The session included the review process; applicants should be aware of likely review criteria (eligibility, alignment with fund goals, feasibility, community benefit, budget realism) and prepare applications to address those reviewer considerations.
